text:
sara: quick follow-up after the v4 rfc thread. proposing an "compat facade" at the ingress layer that performs lightweight payload normalization + schema mapping so clients don't all need SDK updates at once.

mike: ingress facade makes sense for centralized control. worried about hot-path overhead though. what's the perf target?

sara: goal is <=5ms added latency p50 for common mappings. heavy transforms would opt into a background path (async enrichment) where possible.

dan: for Dedicated/Private we should ship this as a deployable appliance (container + small config store). customers can host in their VPC.

sophia: cache implications: transformations change request identity. we need canonicalization step that produces a stable cache key post-transform. also consider cache tagging by transform_version.

raj: thoughts: implement transforms as precompiled wasm modules. tiny runtime, deterministic, safe sandbox. fastest path handles field renames and envelope unwrapping without full JSON reserializing.

leo: telemetry: add headers and spans: X-Compat-Cohort, X-Compat-Version, and a transform checksum. log transformation name to tracing for QA diffs.

mike: rollout plan idea: tenant feature-flag with staged percentages (canary 2% -> 10% -> 100%). include an opt-in header customers can send to test.

infra-bot: scheduled job: create canary cluster "compat-facade/canary" on 2025-07-08T05:00Z.

sophia: tests: maintain a corpus of representative payloads. run v3->facade->v4 path and compare model outputs. flag any semantic drift beyond threshold.

raj: add a transform checksum header (e.g., X-Compat-Transform: v1:abcd1234) so we can detect nondeterministic outputs across replicas.

dan: runbook: automatic rollback if error-rate delta >0.4% or p95 latency delta >15%. also manual kill-switch in console.

leo: security: don't rewrite function-calling or tool-target fields by default. any transformation that mutates those must be explicitly approved and audited. tag those transforms with _safety_review_required_.

sara: agreed 12. default transformations limited to structural edits (rename/wrap/unwrap, envelope migration). customers opt-in for behavior changes.

mike: sample mapping snippet for discussion:

```
# mapping rule: move root.user_text -> input.text and copy meta.session -> input.meta.session_id
{
  "match": {"path": "root.user_text"},
  "rewrite": {"to": "input.text"}
}
```

sophia: metric to add: compat.transform.latency_ms and compat.transform.errors per mapping. correlate with model response divergence metric.

raj: impl note: maintain a small fallback path that shells out to a full parser for odd payloads. keep common-path as zero-copy transformations when possible.

dan: for air-gapped customers supply a CLI binary that runs the same wasm transforms offline for migration testing + a preflight that validates sample payloads. docs + examples.

sara: docs checklist: migration guide, tenant opt-in steps, troubleshooting commands to dump canonicalized payloads, examples for on-prem cli.

mike: next steps: spike wasm runtime + bench, define transform spec, and draft rollout runbook. i'll help with durability/perf tests.

infra-bot: jira created: RED-INF-4299 "compat-facade ingress spike" - https://jira.redwood.example/browse/RED-INF-4299

sara: ok i'll open a short spike PR this week and post results here. objections to ingress-first posture? speak now or DM.
